site.title: Ankole
site.description: Ankole is a self-hosted AgentOS for building your own AI colleagues. They take an objective, not a script: they pick up a job in your team's channel, break it down, run it, deliver it, and you judge them on the result.
hero.subtitle: It takes an objective, not a script. It sits in your channels and hears what nobody addressed to it; a job runs for hours until it delivers; you judge it on the result. The longer it works with you, the better it knows your rules.
hero.stack.label: Runs on
thread.aria: A scene in a group chat: two people settle a rule without addressing the agent, and three days later it delivers to that rule on its own.

difference.title: What separates a colleague from an assistant is not the model
difference.subtitle: Getting AI from “it can answer” to “it can carry the job” means changing how it works, not buying a bigger model.
difference.mission.title: The objective lives in MISSION.md, not in a prompt
difference.mission.body: Every agent keeps three files. MISSION.md says what to achieve, SOUL.md says how to weigh a tradeoff, DESIGN.md says what the deliverable should look like. Edit them whenever you like, and the agent works to them.
difference.shared.title: It works in the team channel, not a private chat box
difference.shared.body: Agents join the channels you already use. Anyone can watch a job, take it over, or correct it, and the agent is there for what teammates say to each other, so you never repeat it.
difference.longrun.title: One job can run for hours, not for one turn
difference.longrun.body: A session wakes, takes new orders, checkpoints, sleeps, and picks up where it left off with its context. A background job runs until it delivers, and a worker restart never drops a job in silence.
difference.judged.title: Measured by the result, not the reply rate
difference.judged.body: Deliverables, decisions, and committed actions stay in a ledger. Streaming shows progress; only what the agent commits counts.
difference.owned.title: The context is yours, not the vendor's
difference.owned.body: Memory, settings, credentials, and audit sit on your own machines. People and agents are both Principals, so the runtime enforces permissions instead of a gentlemen's agreement inside a prompt.
compounding.title: It will not make the same mistake twice
compounding.body: An assistant starts from zero every time: what you corrected yesterday, you say again today. Ankole files every correction into the channel rules and into the skill, and it holds from the next session on. The second run of the same kind of job does not start where the first one did.
compounding.ledger.title: Channel rules · Research
compounding.r1.from: Settled between two people; nobody addressed the agent
compounding.r2.rule: Conclusion first, and never drop the risks
compounding.r3.rule: If the data is not there, say so — never estimate it
compounding.r3.from: Written into the skill after an incident
compounding.r4.rule: Value the HK listing on its own, not with the A-share line
compounding.aim.title: The objective is a file
compounding.aim.body: MISSION.md says what to achieve, SOUL.md how to weigh a tradeoff, DESIGN.md what the deliverable looks like.
compounding.playbook.title: The method is a file
compounding.playbook.body: A playbook settles one kind of job and inherits the hard rules of the skill beneath it: financial models, academic papers, pitch decks, data dashboards.
compounding.review.title: Predictions settle up
compounding.review.body: Research runs in three modes: general argues from evidence, forecast reaches for methods like competing-hypothesis analysis, retrospect returns once the real result is in.
compounding.rule.title: Corrections stay put
compounding.rule.body: The agent writes what it learned as a skill proposal, a human approves it, and it holds from the next session.
compounding.memory.title: Memory gets tended
compounding.memory.body: Brain merges duplicates, settles contradictions, and retires stale entries while it is idle, so an old conclusion never sits on top of a newer one.
compounding.proof.title: The hardest evidence for any of this is Ankole itself
compounding.proof.body: This repository has an agent whose job is maintaining Ankole. Engelbart split work into three levels — doing the job, improving how the job is done, and improving the improvement — and the leverage grows as you climb. Running all three on itself is the only honest way to test the design.
capabilities.title: What lets it carry the job
capabilities.subtitle: One installation is enough: it runs the long jobs, keeps the memory, watches the world outside, and gives each agent a seat.
capabilities.async.title: Long jobs run in the background
capabilities.async.body: Background jobs, schedules, and check back later. A job can run for hours; when it finishes, the agent comes back to the same channel. If a step fails, it says which one, then retries.
capabilities.tacit.title: What the room already knows
capabilities.tacit.body: It hears what teammates say to each other. House rules, who prefers what, why an option did not survive last time — things nobody thought to tell an agent — settle into the channel's shared memory.
capabilities.brain.title: Memory that dreams and forgets
capabilities.brain.body: Brain distills talk into curated knowledge, tidies it offline, retires stale entries, reasons over an ontology, and keeps a model of the world outside. Rows in PostgreSQL are the truth; the Markdown it injects is a projection.
capabilities.research.title: Deep research, and playbooks
capabilities.research.body: Fan-out retrieval, layered checks, competing-hypothesis analysis. Once a kind of job runs well it becomes a playbook, and the next one follows it. You get a cited report, not a confident-sounding summary.
capabilities.browser.title: A browser it can really use
capabilities.browser.body: The runtime owns a real Chromium session and the agent drives it through ankole-browser: read the rendered page, click, type, take screenshots, run a repeatable Playwright script, and stay signed in across steps.
capabilities.skills.title: Skills that improve themselves
capabilities.skills.body: The agent writes what it learned as an overlay proposal. A human approves it and it holds from the next session. It never rewrites itself behind your back, and you can see what changed.
capabilities.multi.title: Many agents, one installation
capabilities.multi.body: Each agent has its own mission, access, tools, memory, and the identity it uses outside. A main agent hands bounded work to subagents and does not sit and wait.
capabilities.enterprise.title: Fits your identity and your IM
capabilities.enterprise.body: Lark, Slack, DingTalk, Teams, and Google Workspace are first-class. Identity comes from the IdP you already run, so outbound identity, permissions, and audit follow the company directory.
usecases.title: Every seat it holds has a number attached
usecases.subtitle: Remote from end to end, a named deliverable, and a number that settles it afterwards. Six examples, not a catalogue.
usecases.research.title: Equity research analyst
usecases.research.deliverable: Company and sector notes, scenario trees, entry conditions
usecases.research.metric: Hit rate and excess return once the call is scored
usecases.cloud.title: Cloud cost engineer
usecases.cloud.deliverable: Spend attribution, right-sizing plans, migration paths
usecases.cloud.metric: Cloud spend per unit of work
usecases.audit.title: Smart contract auditor
usecases.audit.deliverable: Audit report with reproducible proofs of concept
usecases.regulatory.title: Regulatory affairs specialist
usecases.regulatory.metric: First-pass approval rate and rounds of questions
usecases.patent.title: Patent engineer
usecases.patent.deliverable: Prior-art searches, invention disclosures, claim drafts
usecases.patent.metric: Grant rate and appeals after rejection
usecases.marketplace.title: Marketplace operations analyst
usecases.marketplace.deliverable: Ad and restock weeklies, product shortlists
usecases.marketplace.metric: TACoS and days out of stock
usecases.quote: “Hold this seat, use the context you have, and answer for the result.”
bets.title: Five technical bets underneath
bets.subtitle: Actors hold the identity and the life of long work, OTP decides what happens when something breaks, ZeroMQ carries live control, Agent Computer runs the local work, PostgreSQL keeps the durable facts.
bets.actors.title: Virtual Actors carry the AI work
bets.actors.body: A session is a piece of work with an address, a state, a mailbox, a lifespan, and a way back — not a task loose in the background.
bets.otp.title: OTP supervision trees draw the failure domains
bets.otp.body: When an agent hangs, times out, or crashes, Ankole isolates or restarts that branch instead of letting it take the installation down.
bets.fabric.title: ZeroMQ carries the live control
bets.fabric.body: Wakeups, steering, checkpoints, streaming, and backpressure all move through a low-latency router, so you can step in and take over while the agent is still working.
bets.computer.title: Agent Computer is the execution floor
bets.computer.body: The LLM loop, the tools, the files, the terminal state, and the streaming output all run in a Bun and TypeScript computer next to the workspace.
bets.ledger.title: A durable ledger holds recovery and audit
bets.ledger.body: Mailboxes, turns, reminders, decisions, and committed actions outlive the process. Streaming is progress; what the agent commits is the fact.
quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.subtitle: Run it from source, or deploy it with Docker Compose or Helm.
quickstart.source.note: Get the toolchains ready with the installer in the repository, then start the full development environment with bun dev.
quickstart.docker.note: Production on one host: the Compose stack brings PostgreSQL, one Worker, and Caddy HTTPS.
quickstart.k8s.body: The public Helm chart deploys the verified image pair, shared Agent Home storage, and bundled or external PostgreSQL.
cta.title: Give it an objective, come back for the result
cta.body: Ankole is Apache-2.0 open source and self-hosted. Put it on your own machines and keep the context and the audit trail.
